A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Feat2GS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, DTU reconstruction evaluations, feature comparisons, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a cross-dataset performance-correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The feature processing, two-layer MLP, Geometry/Texture/All modes, DUSt3R initialization, optimization, and application variants remain unchanged. Equations 2–5 in v2 explicitly represent freely optimized parameters already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both use LLFF, DTU, DL3DV, Casual, MipNeRF360, MVImgNet, and Tanks and Temples with the same task coverage. The new correlation analysis uses existing datasets and results.

E2.justification: The ten probed VFMs, IUVRGB baseline, and InstantSplat comparison remain unchanged. Both appendices already include the Zero123–SD and feature upsampling versus fine-tuning comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain the same view counts, preprocessing, feature dimensions, MLP configuration, 1K warm-start plus 7K optimization iterations, masking, metrics, and test-time pose optimization. Implementation settings are consolidated in v2 Appendix B without substantive revision.

E4.justification: v2 Figure R.1 adds cross-dataset performance correlations for all three probing modes, supplementing v1's dataset-diversity examples. Existing mode correlations, feature refinement analyses, depth/normal visualizations, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and correlation matrices without seed/run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional matrix extends the existing correlation-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main benchmark tables and appendix Tables R.1–R.6 retain their numerical results. v2 adds correlations in Figure R.1, including LLFF–T&T values of 0.02 in Texture mode and 0.05 in All mode.

T1.justification: Equations 2–5 make the existing multi-view objective and freely optimized Gaussian parameters explicit. This reformulates the previously described optimization without adding substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain label-free geometry/texture probing, comparative VFM analysis, and effective NVS variants. The rewritten conclusion foregrounds correlations, SD color shifts, and pointmap consistency already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets cross-dataset agreement patterns in terms of scene type and complexity, strengthening the rationale for diverse evaluation and aggregate findings. The initialization, lighting, and static-scene limitations remain intact in Appendix D.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the reported code/data status from a future release to available. Existing implementation and hardware details are consolidated into Appendix B; their relocation does not introduce new settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Efros and Leung's 1999 texture-synthesis paper and cites some existing references in additional contexts. The research positioning is otherwise retained, including the 3D feature-fields discussion moved to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: the feature-fields discussion and limitations move into appendices, implementation descriptions are consolidated, and references move before the appendices. The conclusion is rewritten and the optimization explanation expanded.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are extensively rearranged. v2 condenses the main-text DTU illustration while retaining its full version in Figure R.5, moves mode comparisons and failure illustrations to the appendix, adds Figure R.1, and updates Figure 1.

improvement.justification: The new cross-dataset correlations provide additional quantitative support for the diversity argument, and the expanded optimization notation improves clarity. Principal results and limitations are preserved, although several discussions become less prominent after moving to the appendices. The net quality gain is limited but supported.
